Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue reported is that StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml incorrectly converts unicode characters above U+00FFFF into two characters instead of the correct escaped form. The test shows that a high unicode character U+1D362 (COUNTING ROD UNIT DIGIT THREE) is not escaped properly, expecting the numeric entity "𝍢" but likely getting something incorrect.

Inspecting the code:
- The method StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml(String) calls escapeHtml with a Writer and the input string.
- The escapeHtml(Writer, String) method delegates to Entities.HTML40.escape(Writer, String).
- The code snippet for Entities.escape(Writer, String) demonstrates the escaping process for each character in the string.
- The escape method iterates over each char of the input string using str.charAt(i), which means it processes characters as 16-bit char units.
- Unicode characters above U+FFFF are represented in Java strings as surrogate pairs, which consist of two 16-bit chars.
- Here, the escape() method handles each char separately, so a surrogate pair for a high unicode character is split and processed as two separate chars.
- As a result, for the input character U+1D362 (which needs surrogate pairs), this method writes two separate numeric entities for each surrogate char, instead of encoding the correct unicode code point as one numeric entity.

This explains the bug: the escape method incorrectly treats surrogate pairs as separate characters rather than one code point, causing incorrect escaping for characters above U+FFFF.

The root cause is the use of charAt() and char-based iteration instead of properly handling code points using methods like codePointAt and taking surrogate pairs into account in escape(Writer,String).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
